topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines the expected learning outcomes, and welcomes students from diverse academic backgrounds.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of cellular differentiation and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: They frame cancer as an accumulation of genetic and epigenetic changes that disrupt normal developmental differentiation and tissue organisation.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and the benign-to-malignant transition
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the morphological and clinical distinctions between benign and malignant tumors and illustrate how tumors invade local tissues and progress toward malignancy.

topics.label: Neoplasm nomenclature and classification
topics.groupedBecause: It outlines the naming conventions and clinical exceptions used to classify benign and malignant tumors according to their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Pathological mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the local, mechanical, and systemic physiological mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumors cause illness and patient death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence in humans and comparative oncology
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the epidemiology of major cancer types across human populations and compare tumor incidence and vulnerability across diverse animal species.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: They examine initial clinical signs of cancer and evaluate the efficacy, methods, and limitations of population screening programs across various tumor types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture by reiterating the core learning outcomes and directing students to upcoming practical sessions and revision.
